newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: French troops hit back at Bangui army mutineers.
newsitem.headline: French troops hit back at Bangui army mutineers.

text.p: French troops in the capital of the Central African Republic hit back on Sunday against army mutineers who shot dead two of their officers while they were with a multinational inspection team.
Witnesses said French helicopter gunships opened fire on targets in rebel-held areas of the city and the Kassai army camp on the outskirts. Tanks and armoured vehicles moved in.
A French military spokesman in Bangui told Radio France International that the operation was one of self-defence and targeted rebel command posts in the city.
"It's an operation of self defence because we were very seriously attacked as an officer and a junior officer were killed," he said, referring to Saturday's killing.
He said that about 15 mutineers had been detained in the operation in which two armed helicopters took part and that there were no casualties on the French side.
He said weapons had been confiscated.
The Defence Ministry in Paris said the two soldiers had been ambushed and murdered by mutineers on Saturday morning while with a mediating team led by officers from Chad and Burkina Faso.

"In the night of January 4 and 5, around 1 a.m., with attacks on our forces increasing, (our) forces conducted an operation targeting position held by the leaders and authors of these acts," it added in a statement.

The Central African Republic is in the grip of its third army revolt within a year. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, intervened to keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power during the second revolt in May.

Hundreds of people have been killed in violence associated with the revolts which were initially about pay but have turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a civilian elected in 1993 during the impoverished nation's democratic transition.
At least one civilian was killed on Saturday when French troops and mutineers clashed in Bangui after civilian supporters of the mutineers tried to move towards the city centre.
"Ten rebels were killed and 30 were taken prisoner," the spokesman said. "There are no more operations planned for today (Sunday)," he added.
He said French troops seized several weapons including AK-47 rifles, machineguns and rocket propelled grenade launchers.
On Saturday, mutineers had shot dead two French officers while they were on an inspection visit with a multinational mediation team.

Witnesses said French helicopter gunships fired on mutineers' command posts in Kassai army camp and other areas of the city under rebel control, during an operation which began in the middle of the night.

Earlier, a spokesman for the mutineers said that three of their number had been killed in the operation as had seven civilians, including children, around rebel headquarters in the populous southern district of Petevo.
